prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an indoor climbing gym with a near vertical wall on the left (1–3 m away), a ground mat below, a receding corridor in the centre-left background (10–20 m away), and an angled climbing wall on the right (4–8 m away). In the foreground on the right, a standing person in a green shirt and harness is about 2–3 m in front of the camera wearer—just outside the wearer's arm's reach, though the left climbing wall in frame 5 and a low white rope bin on the far right (1–1.5 m away, partly cropped at the right edge) come close to arm's reach—while a second person stands roughly 8–10 m further back on the left and 6–8 m behind the foreground person. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer tilts their head down in frames 2–4 to bring the floor mat and the foreground person's feet into view before tilting back up and turning slightly left in frame 5, making the left wall appear much brighter (closer) and cropping the foreground person at the thighs. Compared to the visually busy, multi-coloured climbing holds and geometric wall paint in the RGB strip, the depth map makes the smooth 3D planar geometry of the walls and the continuous ground distance gradient much easier to perceive. However, the map is unreliable around the foreground person's lower legs in frames 2–4, where their shins merge into the bright foreground floor plane, and in the distant background where people and equipment lose crisp depth boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground person on the right (2–3 m from the camera wearer, facing and looking toward the wearer with hands on hips) and consistently detects the distant person standing 8–10 m away on the left (facing right, in profile to the wearer) across all 5 frames, while also picking up two even more distant background people (~12–15 m away near the centre) in frames 4 and 5. In frames 1 and 5, the foreground person's lower legs are occluded by the bottom edge of the camera's field of view, whereas frames 2–4 show their full standing contour on the mat with the white rope bins to their left and right remaining unsegmented. The map highlights tiny distant silhouettes—specifically the background people in frames 4–5—that are very hard to spot against the cluttered gym background in the RGB image alone. However, the segmentation class labels and masks are highly unreliable for the gym environment, falsely labelling large sections of the angled climbing walls as an 'umbrella' (frames 1, 2, and 4) or 'kite' (frame 5), and misclassifying a single climbing hold on the left wall (~2.5 m away, above head height) as a 'sports ball' in frames 2 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a 2D yellow body skeleton only for the foreground person standing 2–3 m in front of and slightly to the right of the camera wearer, showing their torso facing directly toward the camera and their head tilted slightly downward to look at the wearer. The skeleton shows both elbows bent outward with wrists resting near the hips (within the person's own reach of their harness, while nothing is shown within the camera wearer's arm's reach), though the lower arms below the elbows are missing in frames 1–4 and the magenta hand skeletons are absent across all 5 frames. Across the sequence, the skeleton shifts upward and reveals full legs and feet in frames 2–4 as the camera wearer pitches their view down, whereas in frames 1 and 5 the lower legs are cut off by the bottom frame boundary. Compared to the dark clothing and busy background in the RGB frames, the skeleton makes the exact symmetry of the person's wide-legged stance, shoulder tilt, and torso orientation immediately clear. The map is unreliable in completely failing to detect the distant background people (8–15 m away), omitting the foreground person's forearms and hands in frames 1–4, and collapsing the torso into a distorted, foreshortened box when the person is partially cropped at the bottom of frame 5.
